title: Coherent source fibers of a pushout-stable arrow class
statement: Use quasicategories, coherent functor categories and degreewise simplicial pullbacks from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and cocartesian fibrations from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a quasicategory admitting pushouts, and let $P$ be a class of its arrows closed under pushouts and replete, meaning invariant under equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)$. Let $\mathcal A_P$ be the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)$ on $P$. Source evaluation $p:\mathcal A_P\to\mathcal C$ is a cocartesian fibration: a lift of $u:U\to U'$ starting at $f:U\to V$ is given by a pushout square with bottom arrow $U'\to V\amalg_U U'$. For every vertex $X$, the strict simplicial fiber $\{X\}\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal A_P$ computes the homotopy pullback of $\{X\}\to\mathcal C\leftarrow\mathcal A_P$ in the infinity category of infinity categories. It is the full subcategory on $P$ of the coherent coslice modeled by $\mathcal C_{X/}:=\{X\}\times_{\mathcal C,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)$; its morphisms retain the commuting-triangle homotopies and all higher compatibilities. All categories and simplicial sets fit in a fixed universe, and the infinity category in which the homotopy pullback is taken is formed in a larger universe.

source.place: HTT proof of Lemma 5.5.5.14, first paragraph, printed p. 491: pushout stability gives source evaluation cocartesian and the fiber square homotopy Cartesian; Proposition 3.3.1.3 and Corollary 3.3.1.4 (dually). Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this coherent assertion.

proof.text: Put $A=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)$. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], $A$ and its full subcategory $\mathcal A_P$ are quasicategories. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] to $\{0\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$: $\operatorname{ev}_0:A\to\mathcal C$ is an isofibration, in particular an inner fibration. Given an inner horn over $\mathcal C$ in $\mathcal A_P$, fill it in $A$; the horn contains every vertex, so the filler lies in the full subcategory. Thus $p$ is an inner fibration. Given an equivalence $e:p(f)\to U'$ with $f\in\mathcal A_P$, lift it to an equivalence $f\to f'$ in $A$. Repleteness implies $f'\in P$, and fullness places the lift in $\mathcal A_P$. Its inverse and inverse-triangle witnesses also have vertices in $P$, so it remains an equivalence in that subcategory. This proves that $p$ is an isofibration as well.

source.place: Corollary 4.4.5.3 (restriction is an isofibration); full-subcategory horn and equivalence lifting argument.

proof.text:
Fix $f:U\to V$ in $P$ and $u:U\to U'$. Choose a coherent pushout square with other edges $v:V\to V'$ and $f':U'\to V'$, where $V'=V\amalg_U U'$. It gives an edge $s:f\to f'$ of the coherent arrow category over $u$; pushout stability puts $f'$ in $P$, so fullness puts $s$ in $\mathcal A_P$. We will use the natural mapping-space form of this pushout:
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(V',Z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(V,Z)\mathop{\times}^{h}_{\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(U,Z)}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(U',Z).$$
Here is its justification from the cited statements rather than an extra pushout lemma. Let $K$ be two copies of $\Delta^1$ joined at their source, carrying the span $V\leftarrow U\to U'$. The dual colimit criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] identifies the left side with the space of transformations from that span to the constant $Z$ diagram. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-excision] to the gluing $\Delta^1\amalg_{\Delta^0}\Delta^1$ (the gluing inclusion is degreewise injective). By [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-morphism-square], the transformation space on the first edge is $\operatorname{Map}(V,Z)$, since its formula has a homotopy pullback along the identity of $\operatorname{Map}(U,Z)$; on the second edge it is $\operatorname{Map}(U',Z)$. The overlap is $\operatorname{Map}(U,Z)$ and the restriction maps are precomposition with $f,u$. Excision therefore gives the displayed equivalence, naturally in $Z$ and with these restriction maps.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.5.14, proof, first paragraph, printed p. 491; expanded source-evaluation argument.

proof.text:
For any test arrow $h:T\to Z$ in $P$, write $M_f=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A_P}(f,h)$ and $M_{f'}=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A_P}(f',h)$. Fullness identifies these with the corresponding arrow-category mapping spaces: every simplex defining a map between these fixed endpoints already has its vertices in $P$. By [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-morphism-square],
$$M_f\simeq\operatorname{Map}(U,T)\mathop{\times}^{h}_{\operatorname{Map}(U,Z)}\operatorname{Map}(V,Z),\qquad M_{f'}\simeq\operatorname{Map}(U',T)\mathop{\times}^{h}_{\operatorname{Map}(U',Z)}\operatorname{Map}(V',Z).$$
Substitute the natural equivalence of Step 2 into the second formula, using [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] (with the other two corners unchanged); the restriction maps are those fixed in Step 2. A point of this space is a map $a':U'\to T$, a map $b:V\to Z$, and a homotopy $ha'u\simeq bf$, with all higher compatibilities: the intermediate datum $c:U'\to Z$ and homotopy $c\simeq ha'$ may be eliminated, since the space of a variable endpoint together with a path to a fixed endpoint is contractible. Path concatenation implements this elimination, and shortening the path from its variable endpoint gives the inverse homotopy, at all simplicial homotopy levels. The same description results from $\operatorname{Map}(U',T)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}(U,T)}M_f$, by eliminating the intermediate map $a:U\to T$ together with its path to $a'u$. Consequently the canonical map
$$M_{f'}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}(U',T)\mathop{\times}^{h}_{\operatorname{Map}(U,T)}M_f$$
is an equivalence. The naturality and precomposition compatibility in the cited arrow-mapping formula identify this map with the one induced by $s$; hence the square of mapping spaces for $s$ over $u$ is a homotopy pullback for every $h$. This is the mapping-space condition required by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion].

source.place: Lemma 5.5.5.14, proof, first paragraph, printed p. 491; expanded source-evaluation argument.

proof.text: Step 1 gives the inner fibration hypothesis of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion], and Step 3 verifies its homotopy pullback square for every test object of $\mathcal A_P$. That criterion makes each pushout edge $s$ of Step 2 a $p$-cocartesian edge in the horn-lifting sense. Such an edge exists for every $f\in\mathcal A_P$ and every $u:p(f)\to U'$, by Step 2 and pushout stability. The definition in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] now says that $p$ is a cocartesian fibration, with the asserted pushout lifts.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3, opposite dual, and Definition 2.4.2.1, opposite dual.

proof.text: For a vertex $X$ take $E=\mathcal A_P$, $B=\mathcal C$, $T=\Delta^0$ and $g$ the functor with value $X$ in [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit]. Step 1 proved its isofibration hypothesis; all three categories lie in the fixed universe, while their category of categories lies in the larger one. Its conclusion identifies $\{X\}\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal A_P$ with the required pullback in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. This uses an isofibration between quasicategories, with no Kan-fibration or presentability assumption.

source.place: Corollary 4.5.3.28 and Proposition 4.5.3.15, specialized to T a point.

proof.text: An $n$-simplex of $\{X\}\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal A_P$ is a map $\Delta^1\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal C$ whose source restriction is the constant $X$ simplex and whose vertex arrows belong to $P$. The coherent coslice in the statement consists of exactly the same maps without the last condition. By the full-subcategory definition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], imposing that vertex condition makes the fiber its full subcategory on $P$. At degree one the source side is the degenerate edge at $X$ and the square supplies the homotopy for the triangle; in all degrees the maps on $\Delta^1\times\Delta^n$ retain its coherent compatibilities. This proves the final identification without replacing the fiber by a category of triangles commuting only in the homotopy category.
